sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A., Krishna Kant Tiwari
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant, learned A.G.A. for the
State and perused the record.
2.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in case crime No. 263/2021, under
Section 498A, 304B, 323 Ipc and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, police station Kydganj, District Prayagraj
with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.

entities.text: D.P. Act, police station Kydganj, District Prayagraj
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3.  It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has not committed any offence.
Applicant is husband of deceased.
It was submitted that the marriage of deceased with applicant has taken place about five years prior to the incident and out of that marriage, they have a three years old child.

The allegations of dowry demand and harassment of Vimal Sonkar vs State Of U.P. on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27966140/
1 deceased made against the applicant are wholly false.

sentences.text:
In fact deceased used to talk with a boy,
namely, Golu Sonkar and in that connection a quarrel has taken place on 17.09.2021 and the applicant has informed the police and thereafter both the parties were taken to the police and a compromise has taken place.
In this connection the father of deceased was also informed.

The statement of informant was referred and it was pointed out that the father of deceased was present at the spot before the incident and he has stated that first he went to see the sister-in-law of deceased and when he reached on the ground floor, the deceased was found hanged.
It was further submitted that the minor injuries shown on the body of deceased were result of the incident of 17.09.2021, whereas, the deceased has committed suicide on 18.09.2021.
It was submitted that the cause of death of deceased has been shown asphyxia due to ante-mortem hanging.
It was submitted that the deceased has committed suicide due to the incident took place on 17.09.2021.

Lastly, it was submitted that the applicant is in judicial custody since 21.09.2021, having no criminal history, and that in case, applicant is enlarged on bail, the applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail and argued that applicant is husband of deceased and she was being harassed on account of dowry.
It was submitted that in postmortem report, six injuries have been shown on the body of deceased and the same have not been explained by the applicant.
It is further submitted that the trial of the case is in progress.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

6. Let the applicant Vimal Sonkar involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i. The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii. The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant will not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.
7. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant, in accordance with law.
